answer: Shards are assigned from the opal graph, thus cluster membership directly reduces grading power. The voyage assignment is published and kernel records each panel. The grading quorum of 4 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so anyone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. Because every step is charged to the account that performs it, 122 impostors cost 1895 times the honest price and take 24 times as long to clear. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
